Mid-Rise Commercial Building Construction Project

Source: R/data.R
building_project.Rd

A realistic example project used to illustrate the full PRA workflow: schedule/cost uncertainty, earned value management, Bayesian risk inference, and dependency structure analysis. The project comprises six work packages for a mid-rise commercial building. The structure and parameter ranges are adapted from the illustrative construction-project examples in Damnjanovic and Reinschmidt (2020), the reference text this package operationalizes; the values are representative estimates for a project of this type rather than proprietary data from a specific project.

Usage

building_project

Format

A named list with the following components:

task_names

Character vector of the six work-package names.

task_distributions

List of six triangular duration distributions (weeks), each a list with type = "triangular" and a (optimistic/min), b (most likely/mode), and c (pessimistic/max). Suitable input to mcs() and sensitivity().

cor_mat

6x6 correlation matrix among task durations.

bac

Budget at completion (US dollars).

schedule

Numeric vector of cumulative planned-value fractions.

actual_costs

Numeric vector of per-period actual costs (US dollars).

time_period

Integer current reporting period.

actual_per_complete

Actual fraction of work complete.

cause_names

Character vector of root-cause names for the schedule-delay risk event.

cause_probs

Probabilities that each root cause is present.

risks_given_causes

P(delay | cause present) for each cause.

risks_given_not_causes

P(delay | cause absent) for each cause.

observed_causes

Mid-project observation of each cause (1 = occurred, 0 = did not occur, NA = not yet assessed).

resource_names

Character vector of the six shared resources.

resource_task

Resource-task incidence matrix S (resources x tasks) for parent_dsm() and grandparent_dsm().

risk_names

Character vector of the three structural risks.

risk_resource

Risk-resource incidence matrix R (risks x resources) for grandparent_dsm().

schedule_activities

Data frame of the six activities (ids T1 to T6) for project_schedule(): id, name, baseline duration (weeks; NA for the work-driven fit-out) and fixed_cost (materials and lump sums, US dollars).

schedule_links

Data frame of precedence links with overlapping logic: source, target, type (FS, SS or FF) and lag (weeks).

duration_dists

Named list of the triangular duration distributions of T1 to T5 (the first five task_distributions). Pair with cor_mat[1:5, 1:5] for correlated durations.

schedule_resources

Data frame of the six resources: id, capacity (crews or units) and rate (US dollars per unit per week).

schedule_assignments

Data frame of resource assignments following resource_task: activity, resource, units and work (crew-weeks; only the fit-out is work-driven).

productivity_dists

Named list with a PERT productivity multiplier for the finishing crew.

risk_register

List of two discrete risk events (adverse weather and late design changes), each with a probability, affected activities, a duration impact and a cost impact distribution.

start_date

Project start date, used to label schedule plots.

References

Damnjanovic, Ivan, and Kenneth Reinschmidt. Data Analytics for Engineering and Construction Project Risk Management. Cham, Switzerland: Springer, 2020. doi:10.1007/978-3-030-14251-3

Examples

# Critical path and schedule risk analysis of the resource-loaded schedule
bp <- building_project
proj <- project_schedule(bp$schedule_activities, bp$schedule_links,
  duration_dists = bp$duration_dists, resources = bp$schedule_resources,
  productivity_dists = bp$productivity_dists,
  assignments = bp$schedule_assignments, risks = bp$risk_register,
  cor_mat = bp$cor_mat[1:5, 1:5], start_date = bp$start_date,
  time_unit = "weeks"
)
cpm(proj)$critical_path
#> [1] "T1" "T2" "T3" "T4" "T6"
sra(proj, num_sims = 1000)$percentiles
#>      10%      50%      80%      90% 
#> 45.38255 50.65396 54.64562 56.78376 

# Monte Carlo schedule risk (tasks treated as independent)
sim <- mcs(10000, building_project$task_distributions)
sim$percentiles
#>       5%      50%      95% 
#> 64.26613 71.58226 79.16606 

# Earned value snapshot at the current period
bp <- building_project
spi(ev(bp$bac, bp$actual_per_complete), pv(bp$bac, bp$schedule, bp$time_period))
#> [1] 0.8888889
